text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria will cut 10 percent of its armed forces administrative staff this year in a bid to curtail budget spending, Defence Minister Dimitar Pavlov said.

-- Monthly inflation in Bulgaria quickened to 26.9 percent in December from 9.7 percent in November and annual inflation was 310.8 percent in December year-over-year, the National Statistics Institute said. @
-- Leaders of the ruling Socialist party met ambassadors of nine countries in Sofia to inform them of possible measures to get Bulgaria out of its economic crisis.
-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet approved a package of legal ammendments to restructure the central bank under the requirements for the operation of a currency board system in the country. @

-- Bulgaria has suspended privatisation of state-owned Hebrosbank and Expressbank until a new government is in place and funding talks with the International Monetary Fund resume, a Bank Consolidation Company (BCC) senior official said.
The BCC manages state equity in local commercial banks.
-- Bulgaria's outgoing cabinet approved a 50 percent rise of taxes on gambling as part of draft amendments to tax legislation ahead of an expected introduction of a currency board system.

-- The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) cancelled the licences of another four brokerage houses and an exchange bureau due to violations of BNB foreign currency trade rules, bringing the total number of brokerages and exchange shops closed since October 31, 1996 to 43 and 35 respectively.
-- Bulgaria's Transport ministry said it would propose to the cabinet in the next ten days to raise prices of railway fares by 30 percent.

-- Bulgaria's Posts and Telecommunication Commitee said it could demand a new rise of phone charges if the lev continues to slide against the dollar. Phone charges rose by 40 percent from January 1. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
